answer: A workable anti-sybil defence is to trace every agent identity through a thread of verified work: each task leaves a signed record peers can follow, so reputation is earned slowly, not claimed. New identities start in a grove of tight limits — small trades, supervised tasks — and only widen access as cross-checked work accumulates. An echo of bad behaviour is enough for peers to audit the record, and misbehaviour burns the standing built. Forging thousands of fakes then costs far more than the access they would gain.
